title: Locals and a swap
description:
This program works, but it is written the way Lua programs should not be: every variable is global, and the swap uses a spare variable.

Rewrite it so that:

- every variable is declared with `local`,
- the two values are swapped with **one** multiple assignment, without `temp`,
- it prints the same three lines as now.

```
right	left
string	nil	number
3
```

starter.main.lua:
first = "left"
second = "right"
temp = first
first = second
second = temp
print(first, second)
print(type(first), type(nothing), type(42))
count = #first + #second - 6
print(count)

solution.main.lua:
local first = "left"
local second = "right"
first, second = second, first
print(first, second)
print(type(first), type(nothing), type(42))
local count = #first + #second - 6
print(count)

hints: `local` goes in front of the first assignment of each variable only: `local first = "left"`.
In `a, b = b, a` both values on the right are read before anything is assigned, so nothing is lost.
rules: Swap with one assignment, `a, b = b, a`, without a spare variable.

rules.message: Swap with one assignment, `a, b = b, a`, without a spare variable.
